newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks open sharply lower ahead of FOMC.
newsitem.headline: French stocks open sharply lower ahead of FOMC.

text.p: French stocks opened sharply lower on Tuesday, giving back some of the previous week's big gains, in a cautious consolidation ahead of a U.S. Federal Reserve policy meeting.

Traders said investors were cautious ahead of the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee meeting later on Tuesday, with the market divided on whether the Fed would raise interest rates by a quarter-percentage point.
They said the market also needed to consolidate last week's advance to record highs.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was down 30.05 points or 1.08 percent at 2,754.23 at 0900 GMT while the CAC-40 futures contract was down 27 at 2,753.

"We're coming up to a couple of key events -- the FOMC meeting, the French (parliamentary) election -- and the market's at record highs. It's normal to correct," one trader said. The CAC index rose 5.71 percent last week.

Shares in Danone extended their advance after the chairman's remarks last week that the food group planned to focus on key segments and that it expected higher sales and profits for 1997. The stock was up 0.99 percent at 914 francs.
Renault's stock was down 2.74 percent at 152.70 francs, among the hardest hit by profit-takers.
Profit-taking hits LVMH, down 2.28 percent at 1,454 francs, and Renault, down 2.74 percent at 152.70 francs.
